description.narrative: Building Rural Income through inclusive Dairy business Growth in Ethiopia (BRIDGE+) is a follow-up of BRIDGE program, financed by EKN Ethiopia and implemented by a consortium led by SNV with Agriterra and Wageningen University & Research as partners. BRIDGE+ aims to accompany the take off of the dairy value chain in Ethiopia, benefiting 350,000 smallholder dairy farmers and 4 million consumers, including 1 million schoolchildren located in 10 regions of Ethiopia (Addis Ababa, Amhara, Diredawa, Harar, Oromiya, Sidama, South Central, South Shoa, South West and Tigray). BRIDGE+ goal is to create an inclusive and sustainable dairy value chain that benefits all its participants, with a focus on smallholder farmers within the mixed farming system. While Agriterra was an implementing partner in the first phase of BRIDGE, due to its increased strategic role it is now consortium partner in BRIDGE+. Agriterra will be focusing on building capacities of the primary cooperatives, with particular attention for management and governance, with as specific target increasing the role of women in cooperative leadership; both private sector providers and government agents will be increasingly mobilised in this approach. Agriterra will also enhance the strategic role of cooperatives within the sector (policy influencing) and in the later stages of this phase start providing support to unions (if appropriate).
Dairy Cooperatives and its member farmers

The overall objective of the BRIDGE+ programme is to contribute to a functioning dairy value chain that creates inclusive and sustainable benefits for all its participants, including wider society, with particular focus on smallholder farmers within the mixed farming system. To attain this objective, the project will operate at three levels: (1) smallholder farmers: increase benefits from dairy farming; (2) dairy value chain: improving functioning and food safety; and (3) at sector level: strengthening institutional structure.In BRIDGE+ Agriterra focuses on building the capacities of dairy cooperative societies to deal with the changing market dynamics (including resilience). Agriterra will gradually withdraw its services, by focusing on larger cooperatives (and merging of smaller ones) and building capacities in the private sector and government (Ethiopian Cooperative Commission) at both national and local levels. In the BRIDGE+ project, Agriterra is in the position of dairy cooperatives strengthening the value chain and support services for the cooperative sector locally accessible 150 cooperatives operational, with 100,000 members and marketing 600,000 ltr/day.On IATI, Agriterra will report on three key KPIs:- # of cooperatives supported, - # of Farmers supported- Daily average milk collection volume by supported cooperativesBeyond these three main KPIs, the project monitors 13 additional indicators to ensure progress toward the primary goals.
